strengths: Novel problem formulation: First to seriously address lifelong head avatar modeling from psychology/identity perspective, establishing new research direction with clear motivation
Comprehensive technical execution: Neural parametric model elegantly extends 3DMM principles; Dynamo's dynamic basis pruning is clever; DNA-2DGS design well-motivated for rendering and meshing
Extensive experimental validation: Multiple evaluation protocols, 8+ baseline comparisons, ablation studies, identity consistency metrics, and cross-dataset evaluation (INSTA + TimeWalker-1.0)
Strong quantitative results: Outperforms baselines on primary metrics (PSNR 27.28, SSIM 0.949, LPIPS 0.071); demonstrates successful cross-lifestage/cross-identity reenactment and mesh reconstruction
Substantial dataset contribution: TimeWalker-1.0 with 40 identities, 2.7M frames, diverse attributes (age 20-80, ethnicities, accessories) fills gap in lifelong avatar datasets
Transparent limitations and ethical considerations: Honest discussion of FLAME constraints, view angle limitations, data imbalance; includes ethics statement and data usage agreements
weaknesses: Oversold 'lifelong' framing: Limited to ages 20-80 (not true infancy-to-old-age), celebrities only with curated data; paper positions as 'preliminary exploration' but marketing emphasizes 'lifelong' throughout

Fundamental FLAME dependency: Architecture tightly coupled to FLAME's fixed topology; exaggerated expressions and unseen parts cause visible artifacts; directly limits the claimed 'full-scale animation' capability

Critical view synthesis limitations: Noticeable degradation beyond 45° yaw angle (Fig. 12); this range is restrictive for practical applications (telepresence, archiving); root cause (data distribution) acknowledged but unsolved

Imperfect disentanglement: Lighting separation via residual embeddings shows identity drift and artifacts (Section F.4); authors acknowledge 'disentanglement not yet perfect,' undermining claims of steerable space

Limited generalization: Method is person-specific requiring retraining per identity; celebrities only; data augmentation with large models showed mixed results; scalability to general populations unclear

Experimental fairness concerns: Protocol-2 comparison uses single model (ours) vs. N models (baselines) for N lifestages; GAGAvatar/GPHM comparisons limited (not open-sourced); PAV reimplemented by authors

Insufficient design justification: Dynamo threshold κ selection heuristic; loss weight tuning procedure undocumented; why 2DGS over dynamic 3DGS beyond depth handling not justified; warm-up phase impact unquantified

Narrow experimental scope: Only 5 identities in main experiments; more results in appendix but limited diversity; no user perceptual studies; computational costs (3-5hrs training, 10min/mesh) not addressed for scalability

Incomplete large-scale pretraining exploration: Section I.1 on combining with large models feels preliminary; post-processing and data augmentation attempts yielded limited benefits, suggesting underdeveloped direction
